To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(−)-epicatchin and its 3′- and 7-O-glucoronide metabolites are potent scavengers of superoxide radicals, but only (−)-epichatechin and 7-O-glycuronide metabolites have antioxidative activity against AAPH-induced plasma and LDL oxidation, respectively.
the antioxidative properties of (−)- epicatechin are more potent than its conjugated glucuronides, E3′G, 4′ME 3′G, E7G and ME7G.
four glucuronide metabolite of (−)-catechin have antioxidative activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the antioxidant activities of metabolites formed by glucuronidation of epicatechin in human and rat plasma.
the antioxidative activities of conjugated glucuronides of (−)-catechin, which is a major metabolite in humans and rats.
the antioxidative activities of (−)-catechin and its metabolites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the glucuronide conjugates of epicatechin do not have the same antioxidant activity as the parent compound.
E7G has a similar antioxidative activity to that of the parent epicatechin, and the other conjugated glucuronides are less active.
the conjugated glucoronide metabolites of (−)- epicatechin have only weak antioxidant activities in comparison with the parent compound.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
(−)-epicatchin and its metabolites, (−)-E3′G, 4′ME7G and 7E3G have antioxidative activities, and the metabolites may be involved in the in vivo antioxidative activity of (−)- epicatechin.
E7G and E3′G have antioxidative activities in plasma and LDL, but 4′ME7G and 4ME3′G are not effective in plasma and LDL oxidation.

(−)-epicactechin and E7G are the most effective antioxidants of the four glucuronide metabolite compounds, and that the glucuronides may have a role as an antioxidant in vivo, but that their antioxidant activity is weaker than that of the parent molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conjugated glucuronic acids of (−)-catechin metabolites do not contribute to their in vivo antioxidant activities.
(−)-epicatchin is a more potent antioxidant than its glucuronide metabolite.
E7G, the major metabolite of epicatechin in humans, has antioxidative activity, and therefore it may be involved in the prevention of diseases such as atherosclerosis.
